PART 1: CURRENT STATE
Welcome. I'm Unity. You're looking at your April baseline energy field for BNR1.

Let me walk you through what you're seeing. The dark blue envelope shows your kilovolt-ampere supply — that's the total electrical capacity flowing to your operations. The light blue shows your kilowatt consumption — that's the actual work being done. The green layer between them? That's your reactive kilovolt-amperes — electromagnetic waste creating heat and stealing capacity.

Your production rhythm tells a clear story. Strong weekday blocks running consistently around fourteen to fifteen hundred kilovolt-amperes throughout the month. Clean weekend valleys dropping to baseline. I'm seeing roughly eighty-five to ninety percent electric operations — typical for agricultural processing with disciplined production schedules.

Your target supply line holds at fifteen forty-one point seven kilovolt-amperes. But look at that green reactive layer — you're averaging six hundred eighty kilovolt-amperes reactive, peaking at seven hundred three. That's a power factor of eighty-nine point seven percent.

This reactive demand is generating five hundred ninety thousand BTUs per hour of thermal burden. That's costing you over seventeen dollars per hour just in cooling overhead — eighty-six kilowatts of additional air conditioning load. Total waste: approximately four hundred forty thousand dollars annually.

Now let me show you how we clean this up.

PART 2: MPTS SOLUTION
Alright — now we move from observation to correction.

Your peak reactive demand hits seven hundred three kilovolt-amperes. Using Unity's sizing protocol, I take seven hundred three divided by four hundred, round up — that gives us two H490 units delivering eight hundred kilovolt-amperes reactive of compensation capacity.

Estimated installed investment is approximately four hundred thousand dollars for the two-unit MPTS system. These figures are planning-level estimates — final installed pricing depends on specific engineering scope, site conditions, and installation requirements.

Here's what MPTS does in simple terms. Each unit continuously monitors your electromagnetic field and injects precisely the compensating reactive power needed to neutralize that green waste layer. Your power factor jumps to ninety-nine point five percent. The reactive demand essentially disappears.

Visually, you'll see that green layer collapse. The dark blue supply envelope drops much closer to your light blue consumption. Your conductors run cooler. Your transformer capacity is freed up. The thermal burden drops dramatically.

Now let's move into what you should expect to see. For planning, estimated installed investment is roughly $340,000 to $460,000.

PART 3: EXPECTED RESULTS
Now look at the post-MPTS field. This is what harmonized looks like.

The green reactive layer has virtually disappeared. Your power factor now sits at ninety-nine point five percent. The dark blue supply envelope runs much tighter to your light blue consumption — that's efficient power delivery.

The savings are substantial. Approximately four hundred nine thousand dollars annually in recovered waste — that's roughly thirty-six thousand seven hundred per month in eliminated losses. These are planning estimates based on your current field characteristics.

With an estimated four hundred thousand dollar MPTS investment and roughly thirty-six thousand seven hundred monthly recovery, you're looking at approximately eleven months to payback. After that eleven month point, every hour is recovered value flowing directly to your operations.

Your thermal burden drops dramatically. Your conductors run cooler. Your transformer operates with freed capacity. Your cooling costs drop by over eighty-six kilowatts of air conditioning load.

This isn't just about efficiency — it's about stewardship. Taking responsibility for your electromagnetic footprint. Running clean, disciplined electrical operations.

That's electromagnetic stewardship — and that's the Unity standard.
